mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment signals robust economic expansion, which typically boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 8.0% indicates a slack labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of a low federal funds rate (indicating accommodative monetary policy) and strong non-farm payroll growth (indicating robust labor market conditions) signals a favorable environment for equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS <= 0.2% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month fails to produce positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, strong housing starts (HOUST) and robust GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate an economy approaching its potential, which often triggers central bank tightening and profit-taking in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods classified as late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 700 and GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized), SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals rising inflation, which typically prompts central bank tightening and reduces the real return on equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 95.0 (index 2017=100) indicates a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically reduces corporate output and profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery phase (characterized by high unemployment and rising payroll growth), the improving labor conditions signal stronger future consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods classified as labor market recovery (UNRATE > 7.5 and PAYEMS growth > 0.3% month-over-month), SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.
